### Emulator automation methods

Transport: HTTP POST to `/v1` on `127.0.0.1`; the port is chosen at start (`--port 0` picks a free one).
Every request carries `version` and `method`; optional fields are `count`, `address`, `bank`, `data`, `usagePage`, `usageId`, `down`, `player`; unknown fields are rejected.

| Method | Parameters | Result | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `capabilities` |  | version, methods, maxCycles, maxRead |  |
| `state` |  | cycles (decimal string), pc, a, x, y, sp, p, paused (MIA execution pause), running, stopReason, instructionBoundary, bank (physical ExRAM bank selected by VIA PA0-PA4) |  |
| `reset` |  | state | assert reset for three existing computer cycles, then release; no cold recreation or cycle-counter reset; stop background execution; preserve breakpoints |
| `step` | `count` | state | execute up to count complete cycles; stop when MIA pauses; reject while background execution is running; ignore address breakpoints |
| `readMemory` | `address`, `count` | array of CPU-mapped bytes; null for unsupported side-effect-free reads; no wrapping. Optional bank 0..31 selects a physical ExRAM bank and requires the full read range within $8000-$BFFF |  |
| `input` | `data` | state | inject raw console text bytes through existing MIA input hook; no Unicode conversion or implicit stepping |
| `setHidUsage` | `usagePage`, `usageId`, `down` | state | set or release one held usage ID 0..255 on Keyboard/Keypad page 7 or Consumer page 12; latch transition events; expose virtual device capability; no text bytes or implicit stepping |
| `setHidBitmap` | `usagePage`, `data` | state | replace a 32-byte held bitmap on page 7 or 12; latch changed-bit events; expose virtual device capability; no text bytes or implicit stepping |
| `setGamepadState` | `player`, `data` | state | replace one 10-byte gamepad record in slot 0..3 through existing MIA transition handling; dpad bit 7 controls connection; no implicit stepping |
| `clearGamepad` | `player` | state | release and disconnect gamepad slot 0..3 through existing MIA transition handling; no implicit stepping |
| `video` |  | 68944 numeric bytes of coherent MIA video state; not encoded pixels |  |
| `audio` |  | 80 numeric bytes of MIA audio registers $12000-$1204F, with live sequencer note index and running/taken status at voice offsets 9-11; read-only snapshot |  |
| `run` |  | execution state | start unthrottled background execution; stop before an opcode at a breakpoint; does not clear MIA pause |
| `pause` |  | execution state | synchronously stop background execution at a complete cycle boundary |
| `resume` |  | execution state | clear MIA pause through host resume path, start execution, skip a just-hit breakpoint once |
| `stepInstruction` | `count` | execution state | when not running, execute at least one cycle until next opcode boundary, MIA pause, STP, or count cycle budget; ignore address breakpoints |
| `addBreakpoint` | `address` | unique CPU address array in insertion order |  |
| `removeBreakpoint` | `address` | remaining CPU address array |  |
| `breakpoints` |  | CPU address array |  |
| `clearBreakpoints` |  | empty array |  |
| `addBankBreakpoint` | `address`, `bank` | unique {address,bank} array in insertion order; address must be $8000-$BFFF and bank 0..31 |  |
| `removeBankBreakpoint` | `address`, `bank` | remaining {address,bank} array |  |
| `bankBreakpoints` |  | {address,bank} array |  |
| `clearBankBreakpoints` |  | empty array |  |
| `stackTrace` |  | callers in innermost-first order with pc, bank, and kind (call or interrupt), plus unknownCaller boolean | stop before inspecting; only executed JSR and interrupt entries with verified pushed PC words appear; return frames are removed by matching RTS/RTI; preserved stack bytes are rechecked; unknownCaller remains true because execution before tracing cannot be established |

Limits:

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `maxCycles` | 10,000,000 |
| `maxRead` | 65,536 |
| `maxInputBytes` | 64 |
| `hidBitmapBytes` | 32 |
| `gamepadStateBytes` | 10 |
| `maxRequestBodyBytes` | 8,192 |

Stop reasons: `initial`, `running`, `pause`, `reset`, `breakpoint`, `instruction`, `cycle-limit`, `mia-paused`, `cpu-stopped`.
